messages:
kate: quick check — are we leaning toward a typed-client model (protobuf-first SDKs) for internal consumers, or a single unified edge (JSON-over-HTTP) that does more routing/quotas?

maria: leaning unified edge for DX. fewer client versions to maintain and easy to call from infra that isn't golang.

alex: typed clients give us compile-time safety and smaller payloads (protobuf). makes telemetry consistent w/trace ids propagated in binary. but DX for product teams gets worse.

dinesh: quota/routing gets messy either way. question: do we want routing decisions (tenant routing, model variants) in the edge or in client libs?

jd: edge-first means we centralize policy + canary rollouts and A/B without shipping client changes. big +1 for ops.

maria: exactly. plus console & SDKs can use the same endpoints -> simpler dashboards and alerting.

alex: downside: edge becomes a monolith that needs heavy QA. also extra latency for lightweight calls.

kate: latency concern valid. Typical request budget is 50–100ms p50 extra if we do async routing/enrichment at edge. Can we make it fast?

ops-bot: deploy-note: edge-proxy v2 has 99th latency 12ms baseline in staging.

dinesh: that's fine. but schema evolution is hard if edge accepts typed payloads. protobufs at edge require strict versioning.

jd: client libs with protobufs can embed compatibility helpers, but that's still rollout churn.

maria: what about hybrid: unified edge with an optional typed channel? like HTTP/JSON for most calls, and gRPC for high-throughput internal services?

alex: hybrid is pragmatic. route-by-route: public-facing + third-party -> JSON, internal high-QPS -> gRPC. Need clear conventions.

kate: telemetry implications: two shapes. dashboard needs to reconcile token usage and per-route latency across transports. is that a big lift?

dinesh: we can normalize in the ingest pipeline. add fields: transport=[json|grpc], client_version, route. then dashboards can pivot.

maria: quota model note: tenant-scoped quotas are easiest when enforced at the edge (single source of truth). if clients enforce, we risk divergence.

alex: agree on centralizing quotas at edge. also prefer server-side prefix caching / KV to reduce tokenization cost.

jd: rollout UX: canarying models + config at edge lets product teams flip flags via console without redeploying clients. big win for fast rollouts.

kate: edge responsibility list so far: routing, tenant quotas, canary flags, telemetry emittance, auth checks. client responsibility: validation, retries, local batching.

maria: let's capture tradeoffs in a short RFC. propose matrix: DX, latency, rollouts, telemetry complexity, ownership.

alex: +1. also include a small spike to measure p50/p95 impact for a JSON enrichment step (add headers, policy lookup).

ops-bot: spike-job created: spike/edge-enrichment-latency-447777 on staging.

dinesh: timeline: RFC this week, spike results by next Wed, plan decision then?

kate: yep. I'll draft RFC and link the spike results. cc @maria @alex for review.

maria: thanks — will add examples from console call patterns.

alex: i'll sketch the typed-client ergonomics and example protobuf schema.

kate: one more tiny nit — for hybrid approach we should define fallback semantics if gRPC path fails (client -> fall back to JSON). add that to RFC.

jd: +1. graceful degrade is crucial.

kate: ok pulling this into a short doc. will post link when ready. :memo:
